title: Expiry-Season Reduction Schedule — Lease Term Agreement Renewal Increase Cap
content:
Revenue management sets an expiry-season cap reduction for like-program renewal offer lines on a Lease Term Agreement, by the calendar month in which the expiring term ends: a term ending in November, December, January or February reduces the cap by 0.5 percentage points; a term ending in March, April, September or October reduces it by 0.25 percentage points; a term ending in May, June, July or August receives no season reduction. The cap reduced is the company cap, the expiring term program's renewal increase cap. The reduction never takes the company cap below zero.

| Month of the expiring term's end date | Season | Reduction of the company cap |
|---|---|---|
| January | off-season | 0.5 percentage points (0.005) |
| February | off-season | 0.5 percentage points (0.005) |
| March | shoulder | 0.25 percentage points (0.0025) |
| April | shoulder | 0.25 percentage points (0.0025) |
| May | peak | none |
| June | peak | none |
| July | peak | none |
| August | peak | none |
| September | shoulder | 0.25 percentage points (0.0025) |
| October | shoulder | 0.25 percentage points (0.0025) |
| November | off-season | 0.5 percentage points (0.005) |
| December | off-season | 0.5 percentage points (0.005) |

The month read is the month of the term end date of the expiring term — not the month of the offer, of the handling date or of the renewal's start.

*Examples (hypothetical).* An Extended Lease (13-15 Months) term ending on 31 October: shoulder, a company cap of 7 percent becomes 6.75 percent. The same term ending on 1 November: off-season, 6.5 percent. A term ending on 30 June: peak, 7 percent unchanged.
